prompt:
Research the officially documented limits of Cloudflare Workers on the free plan (requests per day, CPU time per request). Cite Cloudflare's own documentation and quote the limits.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Here's what Cloudflare's official documentation states about the free Workers plan limits. Note that Cloudflare changed its CPU model in 2023, so some older pages may mention a "50ms" cap, but the current official pricing page describes the model differently.

SOURCE: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/#worker-limits | QUOTE: "If you are hitting your daily request limit, you can switch to the paid plan to increase your limit." | CLAIM: This confirms a daily request limit exists for free plan users and implies exceeding it requires upgrading.

SOURCE: https://www.cloudflare.com/plans/developer-platform/ | QUOTE: "100,000 requests per day" | CLAIM: This is the documented request limit for the free plan on Cloudflare's pricing page.

SOURCE: https://www.cloudflare.com/plans/developer-platform/ | QUOTE: "10 ms of CPU time per request" | CLAIM: This is the documented CPU time limit per request for the free plan on Cloudflare's pricing page.

SOURCE: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/pricing/ | QUOTE: "The Free plan includes 100,000 requests per day and 10 ms of CPU time per request." | CLAIM: This confirms both limits explicitly in the Workers pricing documentation.

SOURCE: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/#cpu-time | QUOTE: "Workers on the Free plan have a 10 ms CPU time limit per request. Workers on the Paid plan have a 30,000 ms CPU time limit per request." | CLAIM: This clarifies that the free plan's CPU limit is 10 milliseconds per request.

SOURCE: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/ | QUOTE: "Free: 100,000 requests per day" | CLAIM: This confirms the free tier request volume limit in the official limits documentation.

**Summary:** The free Cloudflare Workers plan officially allows **100,000 requests per day** and **10 ms of CPU time per request**. (The older 50ms CPU limit was replaced by this 10ms limit in 2023 when Cloudflare switched to charging based on actual CPU time consumed rather than wall-clock duration.)
